PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: artifact-hells-chains-instruments-of-bondage-close-up
Workflow profile: 2P39X1 (2.39:1)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Prop/artifact guard: transfer only material response, patina, highlight rolloff, and photographic presentation. Do not add a glowing sword, sacred symbols, blood, or human hands unless this row explicitly requires them.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
HELL'S CHAINS - INSTRUMENTS OF BONDAGE — CLOSE-UP: HERO PROP DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, MATERIALS, SCALE, AND CONTINUITY.

Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Cinematic extreme close-up production still of Hell's chains — the instruments of bondage that hold the righteous dead in the inner prison cavern of the fortress of Hades — captured at the instant before divine liberation, when every link still bears the weight of ages yet one critical ring is stressed to the verge of fracture. The primary subject is a heavy medieval-to-ancient forged iron chain system: massive oval and rounded-rectangular links, each roughly fist-to-palm scale, thick-sectioned metal heavy enough to suggest eternal load and spiritual imprisonment rather than mere physical restraint. Links interlock with industrial gravity; welds are crude hammer-forged closures with visible forge scars, hammer marks, and uneven thickness from hand work across millennia of imagined use. Surface metal is deep charcoal-black and sickly iron-gray underlaid with active orange-brown and green-black corrosion: flaking rust blooms, pitted cratering, crystalline oxide crusts, salt-like white mineral deposits in crevices, and long vertical streaks of dried blood oxidized to dark burgundy-brown and near-black lacquer where centuries of contact with pale captive flesh left residue. Micro-texture reads under raking light: microscopic scale of rust, hairline stress fractures racing across a stressed link, fine powdered iron dust, and cold moisture beads collecting in the hollows of each ring.

Composition locks on a shallow-depth hero zone: one stressed central link and two to three neighboring links in razor focus, the rest of the chain receding into soft bokeh as it climbs or spans across frame. The stressed link shows metal stretched thin at the inner curve, a pale hairline crack glowing faintly with the first cold-blue hell-torch reflection mixed with a distant whisper of golden intrusion light — the visual promise that these bonds will break not gradually but all at once when the Living One passes. Secondary chain strands cross the background at different angles, implying the chamber's suspension grid: horizontal runs spaced like a prison lattice and vertical hangers descending from an unseen ceiling, consistent with the inner chamber's capacity for thousands of souls suspended like marionettes from walls and floors. No living face is featured as a portrait subject; at most a soft, out-of-focus suggestion of pale wrist or ankle skin may press against a link at the extreme edge of frame as environmental context only, never competing with the metal as hero, never readable as a second subject, never modern jewelry or clothing.

Environment is Hell's inner chamber before full transformation: black stone and smoke-choked air, cold blue torch light approximately 2000K raking hard across the metal from one side, with a deep crimson underglow approximately 3500K lifting from the floor plane and a thin distant gold-amber edge beginning to invade from off-frame divine presence. Volumetric ash and fine particulate hang in the air; faint ember dust drifts past the links. Color grade holds the hell-realm palette — deep crimson, obsidian black, cold royal-blue torch spill, blood-rust iron, with restrained amber only as impending hope, not full glory yet. Camera language: macro-to-close-up prime feel approximately 85–100mm equivalent, very shallow depth of field, 2.39:1 cinematic widescreen framing, slight Dutch or low raking angle that emphasizes weight and oppression, production-still clarity suitable as a physical prop reference plate for VFX and set dressing. Materials continuity: pure iron and ancient forge work only — no chrome, no stainless steel, no padlocks of modern manufacture, no plastic, no barcodes, no logos. Sacred biblical-epic tone: instruments of bondage as moral and spiritual weight, not gore spectacle. Neutral production reference framing keeps the complete primary chain segment readable as a constructible object: full link geometry, corrosion map, blood residue pattern, and stressed fracture zone all legible for matching across liberation shots when the cascade of snapping metal thunders through the cavern. No modern objects, no readable text, inscriptions, runes-as-lettering, captions, watermarks, UI, borders, or graphic overlays. Photoreal live-action biblical epic production quality, physically coherent metal response and lighting, accurate scale and materials throughout. Neutral production reference framing, the complete object visible, accurate materials and scale, no labels or text.
